text:
marta: Halcyon weekly health check — quick snapshot for folks. Usage up ~12% w/w and spend +8% (mostly embeddings). Main ask: p95/p99 by route/model streaming vs non-streaming — see highlights below and flag any infra or rollout noise. Link: <https://app.redwood/halcyon/health|dash>

marta: High-level numbers (24h window):
- /chat/complete (streaming, model=rw-medium-1): p95=280ms, p99=1.9s
- /chat/complete (non-stream, model=rw-large-2): p95=450ms, p99=2.8s
- /embeddings (non-stream, model=rw-embed-1): p95=120ms, p99=650ms, errors bumped 0.3% -> 0.9%
- tail spike yesterday at ~2026-02-11 14:23 UTC on streaming /chat/complete p99 +1.6s vs baseline

marta: Notes: no active onboard tasks blocking renewals yet, but the p99 drift could affect latency SLOs for Halcyon's user flows. Putting this here so eng + cs can decide next steps.

ryan: I saw that spike in node-pool-alpha logs — there was a short scheduling jitter during batch reclaim around 14:22. Noticed 3 pods bounced in ~45s window.

jia: +1 to that. When pods bounce we get cold-KV-cache TKs and sometimes routing falls back to rw-large-2 variants; that can blow up p99 for streaming because of reinitializing KV cache and JVM warmups on some models.

jia: Quick suggestion: pin a routing preference for this customer to prefer lower-latency variants and reduce fallback to CPU-only quantized variants while we stabilize pool. Sample config to patch (Deploy config / routing policy):
```json
{ "routing_policy": "latency_preferred", "fallback_models": ["rw-medium-1-q4", "rw-small-1"], "cache_preload": true }
```

health-bot: scheduled-report 1956789200: Automated p95/p99 snapshot uploaded to Halcyon dashboard. Alerts: 1 new p99 deviation on /chat/complete (streaming) above threshold.

marta: Thanks. Also embedding error bump — logs show intermittent 503s from upstream vectorizer service between 02:10-02:35 UTC. CS is capturing impacted customers; Halcyon had ~120 failed embedding calls across that interval.

elena: Hey team, can you confirm whether Halcyon's engineers need to change their client to handle any of these tweaks? They asked about streaming client samples and backpressure handling. :thinking_face: 

jia: For Halcyon no major client changes required for routing policy tweaks. If we change model variants on their route, streaming deltas are identical. But recommend adding a retry/backoff wrapper and handling partial streams. Example Node snippet: 
```js
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-medium-1', route: '/chat/complete' });
stream.on('delta', d => process.stdout.write(d));
stream.on('end', () => console.log('stream ended'));
stream.on('error', err => retryWithBackoff(err));
```

ryan: Action items I can take: 1) Pin Halcyon routing to latency_preferred for next 6h. 2) Force gradual pod drain window increase on pool-alpha to avoid simultaneous restarts. I'll open a small rollout PR and schedule canary.

marta: Perfect. Can we schedule the canary for 10:00 PDT tomorrow and monitor p95/p99 for 2h? Also add a metric watch on embedding 5xx rate.

ryan: Yep — canary scheduled. I'll post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

marta: For CS: follow up with Halcyon for a quick sync — explain we're doing routing pin + infra stabilizer, and we'll share updated p95/p99 snapshot after canary.

elena: Thanks — I’ll set up a 30 min sync with Halcyon PM for tomorrow afternoon.

jia: One more note — if p99 persists after pinning, we should consider temporary KV-cache warmup on new pods for that customer's route. Low-risk: prewarm keyspaces on rollout.

marta: Good call. Adding to post-canary checklist.

health-bot: 1956789399: Canary started (manual trigger by ryan). Monitoring channel: #infra-canaries.

marta: Closing loop here — will drop the updated p95/p99 snapshot once canary has 2h of stable metrics. Thanks everyone.
